works.title: Dual Regulation of Monomer Transport Enables Ultrahigh Mg2+/Li+ Selectivity in Polyamide Nanofiltration Membranes
institutions: University of Science and Technology of China
University of Science and Technology of China , , ,
works.abstract: Abstract Nanofiltration membranes are promising for lithium recovery from salt-lake brines, yet their Mg2+/Li+ separation performance can be further improved. Here, we present an organic-phase engineering strategy that systematically tailors the carbon-chain length of alkane solvents, from n-hexane (C6) to 2-methylundecane (C12), to simultaneously regulate piperazine enrichment at the water–organic interface and trimesoyl chloride diffusion kinetics. This dual regulation transforms conventional rapid and random interfacial polymerization into a more confined and homogeneous growth process. The resulting polyamide membranes exhibit a reduced negative surface charge and a narrower and more uniform pore-size distribution. These structural features substantially enhance Mg2+/Li+ separation, with the C12 membrane achieving a Mg2+/Li+ selectivity of up to 306.6 in the mixed-salt solutions. To assess performance under realistic conditions, a two-pass nanofiltration process was evaluated using simulated salt-lake brine. The C12 membrane increased lithium purity from 2.4% to 97.7% while reducing the Mg2+/Li+ mass ratio from 40 to 0.024. This study provides new insight into the kinetic regulation of interfacial polymerization through organic-phase engineering and demonstrates an effective membrane design strategy for high-selectivity lithium extraction from complex brines.

works.title: Time-aware evaluation of metaheuristic-optimized support vector regression for permeate conductivity in hybrid nanofiltration–reverse osmosis desalination
works.journal: Journal of King Saud University – Engineering Sciences
works.abstract: Abstract Machine learning models of desalination plants are often tested on random splits of time-ordered records, which can overstate their accuracy. This study evaluated support vector regression (SVR) tuned by Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), the Genetic Algorithm (GA), Bayesian Optimization (BO), and Harris Hawks Optimization (HHO) for predicting permeate conductivity in a trihybrid nanofiltration–reverse osmosis pilot plant. Seventy-three published observations of five operating variables, covering about 55 days, were used. All preprocessing and tuning relied on training data only. The models were tested under random, blocked, and chronological validation and compared with default SVR, multiple linear regression, random forest, the training mean, and persistence. Persistence, which uses the last measured value, gave the lowest testing error in every scheme (RMSE 26.6–34.0 µS/cm). No tuned model showed a statistically supported improvement over default SVR. Moving from random to chronological testing raised the RMSE of the tuned models from 44 to 47 to 61–69 µS/cm. In the chronological test, the tuned models over-predicted permeate conductivity by 33–39 µS/cm on average, consistent with sensitivity to temperature values outside the training range. Permutation feature importance (PFI) changed with the validation scheme, and a residual-based uncertainty model underestimated the testing errors. Within the high-pressure period, the five inputs showed weak linear correlations with permeate conductivity, and none of the tested models extracted useful predictive skill from them. Hyperparameter optimization therefore did not improve forward prediction for the dataset. Time-aware validation and simple reference models should be standard in the evaluation of data-driven models for membrane plants. Additional process variables and prospective validation are needed before such models can support real-time operation.

works.title: Life Cycle Impact Assessment of Pesticides Removal from Water Using Nanofiltration and Reverse Osmosis
institutions: University of Zagreb
University of Zagreb Faculty of Chemical Engineering and Technology, Trg Marka Marulića 19, HR-10000 Zagreb, Croatia
works.abstract: Given the environmental burden associated with pesticides, it is necessary to quantify their potential impacts and investigate impact mitigation alongside their removal. Most existing life cycle impact assessment (LCIA) studies lack direct experimental data on residual concentrations, limiting their ability to realistically assess the toxicity-related benefits of pesticide mitigation. This study addresses that gap by linking experimentally determined pesticide removal with LCIA. Three LCIA methods (Environmental Footprint (EF), TRACI, and ReCiPe) were used to evaluate pesticide impacts, as they reflect different global regulations and conditions, resulting in different potential impact estimates. Removal of atrazine, imidacloprid, metolachlor, and tebuconazole from tap water and groundwater was carried out using nanofiltration (NF) and reverse osmosis (RO) membranes. The results showed 81–99% pesticide removal with RO membranes and 27–96% removal with NF membranes, depending on the pesticide. Freshwater ecotoxicity and human toxicity (cancer and non-cancer effects) were quantified for untreated matrices and compared to results obtained with NF and RO treatment data. The findings indicate that NF and RO treatment can reduce calculated pesticide toxicity impacts across the evaluated categories.

works.title: Integrated nanofiltration–osmotic distillation for complete dealcoholization of red wine: Separation performance and product quality
institutions: National Research Council
Institute on Membrane Technology
University of Bologna
works.abstract: This study presents the first investigation of a hybrid nanofiltration (NF)-osmotic distillation (OD) process for the complete dealcoholization of red wine (Nero di Troia, 11.9% v /v), with particular emphasis on separation performance and product quality. The process involved an initial NF concentration step (up to a weight reduction factor, WRF, of 4) followed by three consecutive diafiltration (DF) stages. The permeate from the initial NF step was dealcoholized by OD, and the resulting dealcoholized stream was reused as the diafiltration solvent for the three DF stages. Finally, the dealcoholized permeate obtained from the OD step after DF3 was blended back with the DF3 retentate to restore the original feed volume, yielding a dealcoholized wine with an ethanol content of 0.25% v /v. During the initial NF step, permeate flux decreased from 5.64 to 1.15 kg m −2 h −1 at WRF 4, while higher initial fluxes of 14.0, 11.3, and 23.0 kg m −2 h −1 were observed during DF1, DF2, and DF3, respectively. The NF membrane showed low ethanol rejection (7.1%) and higher rejection (>85.0%) of dry extract, tartaric and citric acid and potassium, indicating preferential ethanol transport. The integrated process reduced ethanol to 0.25% v /v, corresponding to a 97.9% reduction and meeting the European Union criterion for dealcoholized wine (DW). However, substantial changes in DW composition were observed, including a reduction in total acidity (68%), dry extract (51%), and ash content (66%), while glycerol was well preserved. Color intensity decreased by 58%, while lightness ( L* ) increased by 132%. Volatile analysis identified 28 compounds, with an overall loss of 91.1% in volatile concentration. Esters, acids and terpenes were the most severely affected class (>95% loss), followed by alcohols (89.1%). Despite these substantial losses, phenylethyl alcohol, ethyl butanoate, isoamyl acetate, ethyl hexanoate, diethyl succinate, isovaleric acid, and nonanoic acid maintained OAVs ≥ 1 in the dealcoholized wine (DW), indicating that they could still contribute to the wine aroma after dealcoholization. Overall, these finding provides feasibility of integrated NF–OD processing while highlighting the trade-off between ethanol removal and retention of wine constituents.

works.title: Membrane Technologies for the Removal of Bisphenol A from Wastewater: Current Advances, Challenges, and Future Perspectives
institutions: Mintek
University of Limpopo
Sefako Makgatho Health Sciences University
works.abstract: Bisphenol A (BPA) is one of the most frequently detected endocrine-disrupting substances in aquatic surroundings due to its extensive use in the production of plastics, epoxy resins, and consumer products. The ongoing release of BPA-containing municipal and industrial effluents puts ecosystems and human health at danger; hence, efficient water and wastewater treatment methods must be developed. Membrane technologies have become one of the most promising treatment options due to their high separation efficiency, operating flexibility, small size and compatibility with current treatment systems. Recent developments in membrane-based BPA removal techniques, including microfiltration, ultrafiltration, nanofiltration, reverse osmosis, forward osmosis, and membrane distillation, are critically examined in this review. The impact of operating conditions, fouling behaviour, wastewater matrix characteristics, and membrane material features on BPA rejection performance is thoroughly examined. Additionally, new advances in membrane bioreactors, nanocomposite membranes, mixed-matrix membranes, and hybrid membrane systems combined with electrochemical technologies, enhanced oxidation processes, and adsorption are assessed. Key findings show that advanced hybrid membrane systems can improve removal efficacy, lower fouling, and increase process sustainability, whereas nanofiltration and reverse osmosis typically attain BPA rejection efficiency over 90%. Although industrial-scale and hybrid membrane systems have been implemented worldwide for removing contaminants such as BPA, challenges related to membrane fouling, concentrate management, long-term stability, energy consumption, and large-scale implementation remain areas for further improvement. To enable the effective and economical removal of BPA from wastewater, future research should concentrate on the creation of smart and self-cleaning membranes, sustainable membrane materials, AI-driven process optimization, and pilot-scale validation.

works.title: Holey Reduced Graphene Oxide Nanofiltration Membranes: Microstructure–Transport Relations and Enhanced Fractionation of Complex Streams
institutions: Georgia Institute of Technology
Georgia Institute of Technology , , 311 Ferst Drive NW , , ,
Georgia Institute of Technology , , 500 10th Street NW , , ,
Georgia Institute of Technology , , 801 Ferst Drive NW , , ,
works.abstract: Abstract Membranes based on two-dimensional nanomaterials such as graphene oxide (GO) and reduced GO (rGO) are increasingly investigated for nanofiltration applications involving complex biomass-derived streams. However, GO membrane performance is limited by extended transport pathways and restricted flux arising from the tortuous alignment of impermeable nanosheets. We report a systematic study of reduced “holey” graphene oxide (rhGO) membranes, fabricated by controlled oxidative etching of GO nanosheets, to investigate the effect of in-plane nanopores on water and solute transport. Membranes with varying degrees of hole sizes and densities, as well as two distinct film thicknesses (70 and 130 nm), were evaluated systematically for pure water permeation and rejection of ionized and neutral solutes. Concurrently, the microstructural features of the nanoflakes and membranes (hole size distribution, flake size distribution) were characterized quantitatively with extensive AFM and TEM statistical measurements. The membrane permeation and microstructural data allowed the parametrization and validation of an extended transport model that allows the prediction of flux and solute rejection trends that account for the presence of holes in the membranes. Compared to nonholey rGO membrane controls, rhGO membranes demonstrated enhanced water flux and 3-fold increase in throughput during nanofiltration of a complex feedstock (kraft black liquor) while maintaining high lignin rejection (&gt;95%) and similar divalent salt exclusion as nonholey rGO membranes. This study underscores the potential of nanosheet defect engineering as a scalable strategy for tuning microstructure–transport relationships in 2D-material-based membranes for harsh-environment separations.

works.title: Multiscale Intercalation Strategies for Reconstructing Lamellar MXene Membranes
institutions: Zhejiang University , , ,
works.abstract: Abstract Lamellar MXene membranes, constructed by stacking MXene nanosheets to form two-dimensional nanochannels with ultrafast transport and sieving ability, have emerged as a promising platform for molecular and ionic separations as well as osmotic energy harvesting. However, the performance of these MXene membranes is often constrained by swelling-induced unstable nanochannels and monotonous chemistry environments within nanochannels. One of the most effective routes to these challenges lies in the incorporation of functional intercalation matters into the confined nanochannels of MXene, which not only orchestrate interlayer spacing and nanochannel chemistry but also improve stability by forming multiple interactions with neighboring nanosheets. Over the past decade, a series of multiscale intercalation matters have been designed and explored, mainly spanning from ions to small molecules, polymers, and nanomaterials. Despite significant achievements, a timely and comprehensive review that systematically elucidates how various multiscale intercalation matters reconstruct MXene membranes is missing. In this review, we discuss recent advances in intercalation strategies for lamellar MXene membranes, categorized by the chemical nature and dimensionality of the intercalating matters. We underscore their critical roles in modulating both the structural and chemical features of nanochannels, and we systematically analyze the corresponding effects on transport behavior and separation performance. Finally, some key unresolved challenges and future directions are highlighted to guide the design and synthesis of high-performance lamellar MXene membranes.

works.title: Evaluation of advanced three-stage membrane desalination technologies for efficient industrial brine concentration
institutions: a Covestro Deutschland AG, Kaiser-Wilhelm-Allee 60, 51373 Leverkusen, Germany
b TH Köln – University of Applied Sciences, Betzdorfer Str. 2, 50679 Cologne, Germany
c Bochum University of Applied Sciences, Am Hochschulcampus 1, 44801 Bochum Süd, Germany
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Graph of osmotic pressure versus NaCl concentration, showing different pressure-driven reverse osmosis regimes up to saturation. The development of energy-efficient concentration processes is essential to facilitate the industrial reuse of brine. This study assesses a calculated three-stage membrane process, comparing configurations operating at 80 and 120 bar using experimentally characterized, commercially available 4-inch spiral wound membrane elements. Experiments are conducted across a systematic range of NaCl feed concentrations from 60 to 110 g/L and target final concentrations of 220–280 g/L. Based on the experimental results, a process design is proposed, and the energy demand as well as the required membrane area are calculated. The results demonstrate that, under the selected experimental correlations and calculation assumptions, the 120 bar configuration outperforms the 80 bar variant in terms of specific energy consumption and required membrane area, primarily due to reduced internal recycle streams. Across all investigated scenarios, the specific electric energy consumption ranges from 16.5 to 37 kWh/m3 at 80 bar and from 9.4 to 17.5 kWh/m3 at 120 bar. The 80 bar configuration approaches the energy demand of mechanical vapor compression (20 – 35 kWh/m3), while the 120 bar configuration maintains a competitive advantage across all investigated scenarios. The contribution of energy recovery is found to be modest, not exceeding 15%.

works.title: Breaking the “Micro-Size Inversion” Paradox via a Surface-Chemistry-Driven Molecular Sieving Membrane for Ambient Lithium–Air Batteries
works.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
institutions: Nanjing University , , ,
Fudan University , , ,
works.abstract: Abstract Lithium–air batteries suffer from moisture-induced parasitic reactions and electrolyte evaporation in ambient air. A fundamental challenge is the “micro-size inversion” paradox, where H2O (0.275 nm) is smaller than O2 (0.346 nm), rendering conventional size-based sieving ineffective. Here, we report a composite membrane composed of polydimethylsiloxane and fluorinated vinyl-functionalized covalent organic framework (COF-VF) to break this selectivity barrier. By grafting 1H,1H,2H,2H-perfluorodecyl groups onto a vinyl-functionalized covalent organic framework (COF-V), we establish a surface-chemistry-driven sieving mechanism. This design creates a molecular-level hydrogen-bond-repellent barrier that specifically inhibits polar H2O penetration while maintaining high nonpolar O2 flux, effectively decoupling the permeability-hydrophobicity trade-off. Molecular dynamics simulations corroborate this mechanism, demonstrating that the COF-VF exhibits significantly reduced adsorption affinity toward H2O compared to the pristine COF-V. In 40% RH ambient air, the battery equipped with this membrane delivers a discharge capacity of 3596 mAh g–1 and sustains cycling for 2700 h (270 cycles), a 10.8-fold improvement over unprotected cells. Advanced characterizations via DRT and DEMS confirm that the membrane promotes reversible Li2O2 formation and significantly suppresses LiOH accumulation. This work provides a multiscale strategy for molecular-level selective separation in practical energy storage.

works.title: Adaptive Energy Management System for Reverse Osmosis Desalination: Modelling Fuzzy Logic Control for Hybrid Solar PV, Battery and Grid Systems
institutions: Department of Industrial Engineering, Durban University of Technology, Durban 4001, South Africa
works.abstract: The demand for fresh water in coastal regions has increased the energy demand for desalination systems. This study models a hybrid solar PV, battery, and grid energy system for reverse osmosis desalination under realistic solar conditions in Mombasa, Kenya. An adaptive system that responds to real-time irradiance data is modelled in MATLAB R2025a using a five-year hourly solar irradiance dataset from NASA POWER, an internet database with renewable energy datasets. The analysis done determines the control and economic efficiency of using fuzzy logic control that prioritizes solar PV power, battery, and grid and ensures seamless transitions between energy sources. A well-tuned PID controller is compared with the fuzzy controller. The results show that the fuzzy logic hybrid system outperformed the PID controller, achieving near-autonomous reliance on solar PV and battery energy. Solar PV power provided most of the energy to power reverse osmosis, while the stored charge was effectively used during periods of low solar irradiance. The attained specific energy consumption for the reverse osmosis desalination process was 5.82 kWh/m3, which substantially minimized grid energy use, hence reducing operational costs. The findings highlight the importance of intelligent control in optimizing hybrid energy in desalination applications, offering a viable pathway to low-carbon, sustainable freshwater production in regions with high solar irradiance.

works.title: Ionic Liquids and Deep Eutectic Solvents as Functional Interfacial Phases in Membrane-Based Separations
institutions: Facultad de Ciencias, Universidad Católica de la Santísima Concepción , , ,
Gdansk University of Technology , , G. Narutowicza St. 11/12 , ,
University of Valladolid , , Dr. Mergelina s/n. , ,
works.abstract: Abstract In this Spotlight on Applications, we describe our progress in developing membrane-based separation processes in which ionic liquids (ILs) and deep eutectic solvents (DESs) act as functional interfacial phases rather than merely as alternative solvents or extractants. Starting from stability limitations identified in supported ionic liquid membranes, our work evolved toward architectures in which polymeric materials selectively contact, confine, distribute, or stabilize ionic and eutectic liquid phases. We organize these contributions according to the location and function of the active interface: external polymer–ionic liquid interfaces in dense membrane systems; localized ionic or eutectic phases confined within multilayer membrane architectures; distributed polymer–DES domains in dense hybrid membranes; membrane-stabilized contact with mobile immiscible liquid phases; and liquid–vapor–membrane interfaces in ionic-liquid-driven osmotic distillation. Each architecture builds on an established membrane-process category – perstraction, coated liquid membranes, polymer inclusion membranes, membrane contactors, and osmotic distillation – and is distinguished by the location, flow regime, and function of the ionic or eutectic phase. These configurations were applied to fermentation-product recovery, selective separation of target molecules, ethanol dehydration, food concentration, and water recovery from saline streams. Across these applications, performance emerged from the synergistic coupling of polymer sorption and diffusion, liquid-phase affinity, wetting, morphology, interfacial stability, and resistance distribution. COSMO-RS provided a complementary progression from solute–ionic-liquid screening to direct polymer screening and, subsequently, to thermodynamic interpretation of hybrid polymer–eutectic membrane environments. Collectively, these studies indicate that the polymer, ionic or eutectic phase, solute, interface, operating mode, and membrane architecture should be designed as an integrated interfacial system.

works.title: Voltage Gated Ion Entry Into Two‐dimensional Angstrom‐Scale Channels
institutions: University of Manchester
The University of Texas at Austin
Indian Institute of Technology Gandhinagar
Department of Physics & Astronomy, School of Natural Sciences University of Manchester Manchester UK
National Graphene Institute The University of Manchester Manchester UK
Department of Chemistry, School of Natural Sciences The University of Manchester Manchester UK
Walker Department of Mechanical Engineering The University of Texas at Austin Austin Texas USA
Department of Materials, School of Natural Sciences The University of Manchester Manchester UK
Department of Physics Indian Institute of Technology Gandhinagar Gujarat India
Photon Science Institute The University of Manchester Manchester UK
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Biological ion channels with angstrom‐scale (Å‐scale) constrictions regulate key physiological processes by controlling ion flow via stimuli such as voltage gating across cellular membranes. Artificial Å‐scale channels can reveal insights into the voltage‐gating mechanisms, especially the role of geometrical constrictions on ion entry and dehydration. Here, we investigate voltage‐gating in artificial slit‐shaped channels with a height ( h ) of one monolayer of graphene, fabricated from layered materials. In the resting state, these channels exhibit selective ion exclusion while permitting flow for water molecules. Under the influence of high voltage, we observe a transition from an insulating to a highly conducting state, facilitating ion permeation beyond a threshold voltage. Our experimental findings unveil non‐linear hysteretic current‐voltage ( I–V ) characteristics, which we attribute to a confinement‐induced ion‐entry energy barrier involving ion dehydration and electrostatic effects. The applied voltage can facilitate ion entry by modifying this barrier, potentially through partial dehydration or rearrangement of the hydration shell. Molecular simulations further reveal distinct ion concentrations and mobilities inside the channel during forward and reverse voltage sweeps, demonstrating the influence of the structural organization of confined water on ion transport.

works.title: Casting-Derived PVA/PDMS Janus Membranes with Stable Photothermal Conversion for Solar Desalination
institutions: Seoul National University
Advanced Institute of Convergence Technology
Seoul National University , , ,
Seoul National University College of Medicine , , ,
Advanced Institutes of Convergence Technology , , ,
Seoul National University , , , ,
FineNano Ltd. , Rm. 1027, 10F, Ace Smartwing Yeongtong, 253 Samsung-ro , Yeongtong-gu, , ,
works.abstract: Abstract Solar photothermal conversion enables water evaporation and purification through localized interfacial heating, offering a sustainable approach for solar energy utilization. However, integrating efficient solar harvesting, continuous water transport, and structural support within a simply fabricated membrane remains challenging. In this study, a casting-derived Janus bilayer photothermal membrane was developed by integrating a hydrophilic PVA/FeCo@C/CNTs/ACNTs photothermal layer with a hydrophobic PDMS/ZnO nanorod supporting layer. The multicomponent FeCo@C/CNTs/ACNTs photothermal layer provides strong broadband solar absorption and efficient photothermal conversion, while the PVA matrix facilitates continuous water transport through swelling-assisted hydration. Meanwhile, the PDMS/ZnO nanorod layer provides mechanical support for the PVA-based photothermal layer and contributes to the structural integrity of the bilayer membrane during interfacial evaporation. Under 1.5 sun irradiation, the membrane surface temperature reached 83.7 °C, while an evaporation rate of 1.618 kg·m–2·h–1 was achieved under 1 sun irradiation. In addition, the membrane demonstrated effective performance in solar-driven seawater desalination and dye-containing water purification, highlighting its potential for solar-driven water-treatment applications.

works.title: Molecular design of ion-selective polymer membranes for electrochemical water purification and resource recovery
institutions: Clarkson University
Central Electrochemical Research Institute
Academy of Scientific and Innovative Research
works.abstract: Ion-selective membranes enable electrochemical water purification and resource recovery. Effective molecular design must balance preferential target-ion uptake, rapid transport, and limited water crossover under changing feed and electrical conditions. This review examines how fixed charge, hydration, pathway connectivity, and ion-specific interactions govern transport in charged polymers, microporous materials, recognition membranes, selective surface layers, and covalent organic frameworks. Hydration reshapes transport pathways, making their hydrated dimensions and connectivity more informative than dry pore size alone. Strong binding can favor uptake while slowing release and passage, so selective uptake need not yield selective flux. Designs that partly decouple charge density from swelling or binding affinity from mobility offer ways to balance discrimination and throughput. Practical deployment requires reproducible selectivity, resistance, and water-transport properties across large-scale membrane production. Transport-state retention then requires maintaining these properties as polymer chemistry, hydration, and interfaces evolve during operation. Evaluating them together connects molecular design, manufacturing quality, and durability to current efficiency, product purity, concentration, recovery, and energy consumption in complex feeds.

works.title: Closed-Loop Fabrication of Regenerated Cellulose Battery Separator via Solvent-Guided Structural Regulation
institutions: Zhejiang A&F University , , ,
Everrising Holdings (Japan) Co., Ltd. , 1-23 Toranomon , , ,
works.abstract: Abstract The development of battery separators derived from renewable feedstocks that can simultaneously achieve high porosity, robust mechanical strength, excellent thermal stability, reliable electrochemical performance, and satisfactory environmental sustainability remains a core challenge in the field of sustainable energy storage material. Herein, we report a regenerated cellulose membrane prepared through a dissolution/regeneration process using lithium bromide Molecular dynamics simulation results show that water is the effective antisolvent for driving the formation of cellulose–cellulose H-bonds, yielding cellulose with a better crystalline structure. Subsequently, tert-butanol was utilized to replace water in the cellulose membrane precursor prior to drying, preventing capillary-induced pore collapse. This membrane exhibits high porosity of 70.1%, excellent electrolyte uptake capacity of 243.7%, ionic conductivity of 0.77 mS/cm, excellent thermal stability (no shrinkage at 150 °C), and roust mechanical strength. The Na/HC half-cells assembled with this membrane displays high cycle capacity retention rate of 87.1% at 0.1 C after 500 cycles, which is comparable to commercial separators. This membrane fabrication process enables closed-loop solvent recycling, and the membrane fully degraded after 4 months of soil burial, and life cycle assessment indicated lower impacts than commercial battery separators. These results establish a practical closed-loop strategy for sustainable, high-performance battery separators.

works.title: Genome-wide identification of the rice NPF family reveals OsNPF6.2 as a negative regulator of hypoxic germination via ABA-mediated stress adaptation
institutions: Northeast Agricultural University
works.abstract: Submergence-induced hypoxic stress is a major abiotic stress that constrains seed germination and seedling establishment rate in direct-seeded rice. As one of the largest families of transmembrane transporters in plants, the Nitrate Transporter 1/Peptide Transporter Family (NPF) family is widely involved in nutrient transport and stress responses; however, its function and regulatory mechanism in hypoxic germination of rice ( Oryza sativa L. ) remain unclear. In this study, the candidate gene OsNPF6.2 was screened from 78 NPF family members through genome-wide analysis. This gene exhibits a temporal expression pattern in coleoptiles under hypoxic stress, characterized by downregulation in the early stage, upregulation to a peak in the middle-late stage, and a subsequent decline. Functional verification demonstrated that OsNPF6.2 is associated with negative regulation of the hypoxic germination process in rice, and the coleoptile length of mutants was significantly greater than that of the wild type. Physiological measurements combined with transcriptomic analysis suggest that OsNPF6.2 is associated with the regulation of hypoxic germination through energy metabolism, redox homeostasis, and phytohormone signal transduction pathways, with abscisic acid (ABA) accumulation potentially serving as a stress-adaptive signal. Moreover, this gene exhibits abundant natural variation and subpopulation differentiation in cultivated rice.

works.title: Electrodialysis Treatment of Nitrate‐Contaminated Groundwater Using Modified Cation‐Exchange Membranes
institutions: Aristotle University of Thessaloniki
Centre for Research and Technology Hellas
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Nitrate contamination in drinking water remains a significant concern for the scientific community, particularly in agricultural regions where concentrations often exceed regulatory limits. In this context, selective electrodialysis offers a promising alternative by enabling targeted removal of nitrates while preserving useful hardness ions. In this study, commercially available anion and cation exchange membranes were evaluated for their ion removal and energy consumption performance to select the optimal cation exchange membrane (CEM) for reducing divalent ion depletion using polyethyleneimine (PEI) crosslinked with glutaraldehyde (GA). A systematic investigation of key modification parameters was followed, including casting with PEI of different molecular weights, rinsing after casting, GA concentration, crosslinking time, and different pH values. The resulting membranes were characterized using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS), and cyclic voltammetry (CV), and their performance was tested in treating nitrate‐contaminated groundwater. The optimal modification pathway demonstrated reduced divalent‐ion depletion, achieving maximum nitrate removal (99%) and low energy consumption (0.43 kWh/m 3 ). Stability and regeneration experiments showed a partial and temporary recovery of divalent‐ion retention, with the strongest improvement observed after acidic regeneration. Post‐operation SEM and EDS analyses revealed a Mg‐rich surface deposition, suggesting that it might contribute to performance deterioration.

works.title: Synergistic Bifunctional Design Toward Highly Ion-Conductive Polyamide Composites Ion-Solvating Membranes for Lithium Batteries
institutions: Institute of Coal Chemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences , , ,
University of Chinese Academy of Sciences , , ,
Guangdong University of Petrochemical Technology , , ,
Shenzhen University of Advanced Technology , , ,
works.abstract: Abstract Achieving high room-temperature ionic conductivity without sacrificing mechanical and thermal stability remains a central challenge for polyamide-based ion-solvating membranes (ISMs). Herein, we develop a rigid−flexible coordination strategy by incorporating controlled amounts of flexible aromatic ether linkages into a rigid fluorinated aromatic polyamide backbone. The amide-rich aromatic framework provides mechanical and thermal robustness, whereas the ether-containing segments regulate chain packing, Lewis-basic coordination-site density, and LiTFSI dissociation. Systematic comparison of PA-TFDB, PA-6FODA, and PA-6FAPB demonstrates that Li+ transport does not increase monotonically with ether content but instead reaches a maximum at an intermediate rigid−flexible balance. The optimized PA-6FODA-40-ISM exhibits an ionic conductivity of 9.18 × 10−4 S cm−1, representing a 2.4-fold enhancement over PA-TFDB-40-ISM, together with a Li+ transference number of 0.72, an apparent migration activation energy of 0.0402 eV, and oxidative stability up to 4.95 V. Raman analysis reveals a free-TFSI– fraction of 64% in PA-6FODA-40-ISM, compared with 46% in PA-6FAPB-40-ISM and 37% in PA-TFDB-40-ISM. Combined X-ray diffraction, spectroscopic, and density functional theory analyses indicate that the balanced rigid−flexible architecture produces less organized chain packing and a heterogeneous Li+-binding-energy landscape, thereby promoting salt dissociation and facilitating Li+ exchange between polymer and solvent coordination environments. In contrast, insufficient ether coordination favors contact ion pairs, whereas excessive ether-site density is accompanied by stronger coordination and increased ion aggregation. PA-6FODA-40-ISM simultaneously retains a tensile strength of 43 MPa, an elongation at break of 112%, and dimensional stability at 160 °C. The Li∣PA-6FODA-40-ISM∣Li symmetric cell maintained stable cycling for 250 h at 0.1 mA cm−2 and 0.1 mAh cm−2, while LFP∥Li cells retain 83% of their initial capacity after 300 cycles at 0.5 C. These findings establish rigid−flexible coordination as an effective molecular design principle for balancing ion transport, structural robustness, and interfacial stability in aromatic polyamide ISMs.

works.title: Scale‐Expandable All‐Wood‐Based Hydrogel for Highly Efficient Desalination Enabled by 3D Printing and Array Design
institutions: School of Chemical Engineering University of Chinese Academy of Sciences Beijing People's Republic of China
School of Chemical Sciences University of Chinese Academy of Sciences Beijing People's Republic of China
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Fully utilizing all components of waste biomass while enabling scalable structural design remains a critical challenge for solar‐driven interfacial desalination. Herein, we convert waste wood powder into an all‐component wood based (all‐wood‐based) hydrogel (AWH) solar evaporator via one‐step reusable ionic compounds (ICs) composed of ZnCl 2 and CaCl 2 , and through 3D printing and array design, a scale‐expandable pyramid‐structure array evaporator for efficient desalination was realized. Unlike common methods that need specified component extraction or removal, this IC strategy simultaneously dissolves and regenerates the three primary wood components (cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin). The AWH achieves a remarkable solar evaporation rate of 2.94 kg m − 2 h − 1 and a good solar energy‐to‐vapor efficiency of 96.81%, enabling stable long‐term desalination without salt accumulation. Even after 96 h evaporation, it can still maintain an evaporation rate of 2.53 kg m − 2 h − 1 . Furthermore, a pyramid‐shaped AWH evaporator obtained by 3D printing demonstrates a high evaporation rate of 3.45 kg m − 2 h − 1 , and its 3×3 pyramid‐shaped array achieves a remarkable evaporation rate of 3.33 kg m − 2 h − 1 even by creating a T‐shaped high‐speed steam flow channel above the array. This eco‐friendly and scalable wood‐based hydrogel offers a viable approach to addressing global water scarcity.

works.title: The Nexus Between Heat and Vacuum Pumps: A Novel Hybrid Desalination System
institutions: Department of Industrial Thermal Power Engineering, South Ural State University (National Research University), 454080 Chelyabinsk, Russia
Department of Electric Power Generation Stations, Network and Supply-Systems, South Ural State University (National Research University), 454080 Chelyabinsk, Russia
works.abstract: The thermal vacuum distillation of seawater, preheated by a hybrid solar heat pump, is a candidate technology for autonomous and hot-climate sites, but experimental energy and exergy data for it are scarce. The objective of this study is to determine the energy and exergy characteristics of a laboratory vacuum distiller and to describe them with a semi-empirical model whose validity limits are stated explicitly. A 5 L batch distiller was tested at four temperature/pressure regimes (75 °C/0.4 atm, 85 °C/0.6 atm, 90 °C/0.7 atm and 100 °C/1 atm). The model combines empirical correlations for heating and maintenance energies with an evaporation fraction; this is calibrated on the four regimes and restricted to physically admissible conditions. The productivity increased from 125 to 334 g/h, and the specific energy consumption was 3.8–5.7 Wh/g. The vacuum regime had the highest specific energy consumption (5.7 Wh/g against 3.8–4.1 Wh/g at 85–100 °C), so no energy advantage of vacuum operation was demonstrated. The calibrated model reproduced measured productivity and total energy values within 2.7% and 4.5%, respectively; leave-one-out cross-validation gave errors up to 94%, so the predictive capability of the model is limited and the model should be regarded as a descriptive fit of the four measured regimes. The eight model parameters were fitted to twelve measured values, and no independent validation data were available. The effect of pressure cannot be separated from that of temperature, because the two variables increase together (correlation coefficient, 0.99). The exergy efficiency was 1.6–3.2%: 93.8–95.8% of the fuel exergy was destroyed by irreversibilities and 2.6–3.1% was lost with the residual hot water; 41–44% of the exergy destruction occurred in the heating stage. Relative to the minimum work of separation, the second-law efficiency was only 0.014–0.020%. The measured energy inputs exclude the heat pump and the photovoltaic–thermal panel; therefore, the benefit of renewable-energy integration is prospective and was not quantified. Scientific novelty: This study conducts a combined experimental, semi-empirical and exergy assessment of the thermal vacuum distillation of seawater preheated by a hybrid solar-powered heat pump, with explicitly defined model validity limits. Practical contribution: This study presents laboratory-scale reference values of the specific energy consumption and exergy efficiency of the model, and identifies the main loss sources for the design of an industrial prototype. The delivery of distilled water to remote areas by unmanned aerial vehicles is considered only as a prospective application and was not studied.

works.title: 3D Solar‐Driven Interfacial Evaporator Based on Tailored TiO <sub>2</sub> Nanotube Arrays by Wireless Anodizing for Efficient Desalination
institutions: Shanghai Maritime University
Shanghai Ship and Shipping Research Institute
College of Ocean Science and Engineering Shanghai Maritime University Shanghai People's Republic of China
Merchant Marine College Shanghai Maritime University Shanghai People's Republic of China
Shanghai Ship and Shipping Research Institute Co., LTD. Shanghai People's Republic of China
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Solar‐driven interfacial evaporation is an energy‐efficient desalination strategy. However, the existing solar‐driven interfacial evaporators mostly rely on a surface‐localized photothermal layer for heat confinement, which limits evaporation exclusively to the top surface. The internal transfer channels and potential evaporation area remain unexplored, restricting water production rates. Here, a wireless anodization with a composite bipolar electrode has been proposed to prepare completely internal anodized porous Ti with TiO 2 nanotube (TNT) arrays, serving for 3D solar‐driven interfacial evaporation. By regulating the reaction area and intensity, the TiO 2 nanotubes (TNTs) with tailored size (diameter of 120–170 nm, length of 3–10 µm) have successfully anisotropically grown on the porous Ti substrates, constructing internal interconnected channels. The obtained wireless anodized porous Ti (WAPT) possessed an increased surface area of 7.938 m 2 ·g −1 , as well as solar absorbance >80%, superhydrophilicity (totally wetting within 10 s), and low evaporation enthalpy (451.83 kJ·kg −1 ), making efficient water evaporation with larger evaporation area and lower energy consumption possible. Under one‐sun irradiation, the WAPT showed an evaporation rate of 1.68 kg·m −2 ·h −1 with no salt crystallization and could maintain over 30 days. By assembling the WAPTs into a 3D interfacial evaporator, cooperated with wind‐driven cold evaporation, the maximum evaporation rate reached 2.412 kg·m −2 ·h −1 . In outdoor conditions (solar intensity of 0.6 kW·m −2 at 12 pm), the water collection rate reached 1.59 kg·m −2 ·h −1 . This work should make possible the development of a high‐performance solar‐driven interfacial evaporator for various applications.

works.title: 3D-Printed Photocatalytic Spacers for Fouling Control and Pollutant Degradation in Membrane Water Treatment: Design Strategies and Prospects for Electrodialysis and Nanofiltration
institutions: Lund University
University of Ghana
Division of Chemical Engineering, Department of Process and Life Science Engineering, Lund University, Naturvetarvägen 14, 221 00 Lund, Sweden
Department of Materials Science and Engineering, School of Engineering Sciences, University of Ghana, Accra, P.O. Box LG 77, Ghana
works.abstract: Feed spacers are indispensable components of aqueous membrane processes, but conventional fabrication methods such as extrusion and injection moulding constrain spacer geometry to simple net-type designs, limiting further gains in mass transfer and fouling control. Additive manufacturing (3D-printing) has relaxed these geometric constraints and, more recently, enabled the integration of photocatalytic functionality directly onto the spacer structure, allowing a single component to simultaneously provide mechanical support, hydrodynamic mixing, and in situ pollutant degradation. This review describes the fundamentals of spacer hydrodynamics, including the roles of filament diameter, mesh angle, porosity, and channel height in governing concentration and temperature polarization before surveying the photocatalytic materials, such as TiO2, g-C3N4, iron oxides/oxyhydroxides, metal-organic frameworks and conducting polymers, and synthesis routes (hydrothermal, sol-gel/dip-coating, in situ polymerization, microwave-assisted) used to functionalize 3D-printed spacers. NF and ED are selected as the two spacer-dependent processes most widely used in water treatment and are discussed separately because of their different driving forces. Design strategies for integrating photocatalysts onto printed spacer architecture, the resulting fouling-control mechanisms, and reported performance in electrodialysis and nanofiltration systems are critically assessed, alongside emerging cross-cutting applications. Because direct data on photocatalytic spacers in NF and ED are still scarce, results obtained with spacers are distinguished from extrapolations from photocatalytic membrane studies. Key challenges, specifically photocatalyst loading stability under prolonged operation and light delivery within enclosed membrane modules, are identified among the principal barriers to scale-up, while 4D-printed stimulus responsive spacers, machine-learning-guided geometry optimization, and photothermal-photocatalytic coupling are highlighted as promising future directions. Furthermore, 3D-printed photocatalytic spacers represent a convergent technology capable of simultaneously addressing concentration polarization, organic fouling, biofouling, and micropollutant degradation within a single structural component. Three-dimensional-printed photocatalytic spacers may contribute to the mitigation of concentration polarization, organic fouling, biofouling, and micropollutant degradation within a single component, although these phenomena are governed by different mechanisms and their simultaneous control involves design trade-offs.

works.title: Seawater Desalination in the Middle East and North Africa: Environmental Impacts of Brine Discharge, Energy Use and Pathways to Sustainable Expansion in Egypt
works.abstract: Desalination has become indispensable to water security in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA), which produces almost half of the world's desalinated water. Egypt, facing a widening gap between Nile supply and demand, plans to expand seawater desalination from about 1.2–1.4 million m³ per day today to several million m³ per day within a decade. This review synthesises evidence on the environmental impacts of desalination, with emphasis on brine discharge, chemical additives, intake effects and energy use, and on management options relevant to Egypt's Mediterranean and Red Sea coasts. Globally, about 15,900 plants produce some 95 million m³ per day of fresh water and about 142 million m³ per day of brine, of which about 70% is produced in MENA. Brine, typically with roughly twice the salinity of seawater and containing antiscalants, coagulants and cleaning chemicals, can form dense plumes that affect seagrasses, corals and benthic communities near outfalls, particularly in poorly flushed embayments. Intakes cause impingement and entrainment of marine organisms, and energy use, still dominated by fossil fuels, generates substantial greenhouse-gas emissions. The review shows that most impacts can be reduced through careful site selection, subsurface intakes, diffuser outfalls, environmental monitoring, renewable energy and emerging brine-valorisation technologies, and proposes guidelines for Egypt's expansion, particularly to protect the Red Sea's coral reefs.

works.title: An Integrated Hydrogen Cascade Reactor for Formic Acid Dehydrogenation, Membrane Purification, and On‐Demand Hydrogenation
institutions: Kumamoto University
Institute of Industrial Nanomaterials, Kumamoto University
National Institute for Materials Science
Chulalongkorn University
works.abstract: ABSTRACT We report an integrated hydrogen cascade reactor that couples formic acid dehydrogenation, selective H 2 separation, and downstream hydrogenation within a single system. A redox‐active bimetallic PdNi‐chloranilate (PdNiCA) metal–organic framework (MOF) catalyst enabled H 2 generation from formic acid under mild conditions, while a mixed‐conducting graphene oxide membrane selectively transported hydrogen and effectively suppressed CO 2 permeation. The separated H 2 was directly supplied to a downstream reaction chamber without intermediate storage or external purification and used for nitroarene hydrogenation under ambient conditions. Representative nitroarenes were converted to the corresponding anilines with conversions of up to 99%, demonstrating that the membrane‐delivered hydrogen was sufficiently reactive for downstream chemical transformation. By integrating H 2 production, purification, and utilization within a single architecture, this system offers a low‐temperature strategy for on‐demand hydrogen utilization and highlights the potential of membrane‐integrated reactors for sustainable hydrogen‐driven synthesis.
